newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti 1996 net loss 915 billion lire.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti 1996 net loss 915 billion lire.

text.p: Italy's information technology group Olivetti on Tuesday reported a net loss for 1996 of 915 billion lire as annual sales fell 14.6 percent to 8.304 trillion lire.

A company statement said the group's net financial requirement at end-1996 was 2.197 trillion lire, while adding that first quarter 1997 results were in line with budget projections. It said parent company Olivetti SpA had set a extraordinary general meeting to approve a proposal to reduce the share capital.

Olivetti said the 1996 net loss of 915 billion lire included provisions of 208.7 billion lire for "future expenses and risks" of which 59.5 billion lire was provided for first- quarter losses at Olivetti Personal Computers, which the company agreed to sell at the end of January 1997.

The statement said gross margins declined from 1995 with the downturn stronger in the second half of 1996, particularly with regard to the profitability of personal computers and printers. Extraordinary costs were reported for 1996 of 154.4 billion lire of which 87 billion lire related to payroll reductions.

Olivetti intends to convene an extraordinary general meeting of its parent company Olivetti SpA to approve the reduction of the nominal unit value of its common and preferred shares to 640 lire per share from 1,000 lire currently.
